  crystal_lane_v49.{tmbc,json}: the one fixture written at the pinned
  reader's wire version when the pin moved to trust-ir
  794227ad0df4656634a7906825e242e0edc20aa1 (2026-09-26). No trust-ir
  conformance fixture is newer than v46 at that commit, so this one is
  GENERATED, not vendored: a hand-authored JSON module (one `ungated` bodied
  function whose body is a (i64, i64) `Const` with an unwritten lane, a
  `drop i64`, and a `cmpxchg weak`) converted by that commit's own CLI,
  built from `git archive 794227ad` with `targo --unverified build --locked
  -p trust-ir-cli`:
    trust-ir convert --from json --to bin authored.json crystal_lane_v49.tmbc
    trust-ir convert --from bin --to json crystal_lane_v49.tmbc crystal_lane_v49.json
  The .tmbc header is v49; the JSON twin is the CLI's conversion of those
  bytes and equals the authored module. `trust-ir validate` at that commit
  reports it well-formed (v41 producer rule checked): the validator accepts
  all three constructs. The trust-cg CLI refuses it, from binary and JSON
  alike, by the codegen license (`body_gate: ungated`), which it checks
  first; the adapter floor's by-name refusal of each construct
  (AdapterError::UnmodeledTrustIrConstruct) is pinned by trust-cg-lower
  tests/pin_move_floor.rs.

When the trust-ir pin moves, re-vendor conformance/ from the new pin and
refresh this list; when the new pin's writer is newer than every vendored
fixture, regenerate pinned_writer/ with that pin's CLI. Do it before the move:
scripts/bump_trust_ir_pin.py runs both container targets as guards and rolls
back a move that leaves them red, and the codegen target's
the_vendored_conformance_fixtures_are_the_pinned_corpus_bytes requires
conformance/ (compat_v22_composition.tmbc aside) to be exactly the pinned
corpus's top-level .tmbc goldens with their .json twins, byte for byte
(decision record LD-84).
